chapters.chapter_blurb: How many households and how many women and men were interviewed, and how much of the sample was reached.
Homes, cooking, possessions, who lives in them, and how births and deaths are registered.
Age, schooling, literacy, media, migration and standing with the Social Health Authority.
When women marry, whether the union is registered, and when sexual activity begins.
How many children women have, how far apart, how young they start, how pregnancies end.
The family women say they want, against the one they have.
Methods known and used, where they come from, and how much need is still unmet.
Deaths in the first weeks, months and years of life, and the risks behind them.
Care through pregnancy, at the birth, and in the weeks after.
Size at birth, vaccination, and how families treat a cough, a fever or diarrhoea.
Growth monitoring, breastfeeding, what young children eat, and supplements.
Mosquito nets, who sleeps under them, prevention in pregnancy, and treating fever.
Drinking water, toilets, waste, handwashing and menstrual hygiene.
Abuse, harassment and threats carried out through phones and the internet, who experiences them and what is done about it.
Death rates among adults of working age, and the maternal mortality ratio.
